newsitem.title: USA: Grounded freighter delays 13 ships in Mississippi.
newsitem.headline: Grounded freighter delays 13 ships in Mississippi.

text.p: Six inbound and seven outbound deep-draft ships have been delayed below Boothville, La., after a freighter grounded at the mouth of the Mississippi River, an Associated Branch Pilots dispatcher said on Thursday.

The river was closed at Southwest Pass early Thursday after Norwegian-flagged Ariel, a coal freighter steaming for the United Kingdom, grounded on a mud lump in the swirling waters of the swollen river, the Coast Guard said.
Southwest Pass is the only river entrance for deep draft vessels.
Rising waters have contributed to three accidents that have closed sections of the river this week.

In addition to the grounded freighter, crews are working to secure 100 barges that broke free at Laplace, upriver from New Orleans. That accident shut down the river between mile 120 and mile 132 at midnight.

At Baton Rouge, the river is open during daylight hours to north- and south-bound traffic on a one-way, one vessel at a time basis past a barge that capsized Monday. The barge, part of a tow of 25 barges that hit a bridge at Baton Rouge and broke loose, contains a volatile mix of benzene and gasoline.
